spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Seats, MaxBlock, MaxTTL

VARIABLES free, leased, enrolled, ttl, inflight

vars == <<free, leased, enrolled, ttl, inflight>>

Releases == [node : Nodes, amt : 1 .. MaxBlock]
Lapsed == {n \in Nodes : ttl[n] = 0 /\ leased[n] > 0}

RECURSIVE LeasedIn(_)
LeasedIn(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN leased[x] + LeasedIn(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in 0 .. Seats
    /\ leased \in [Nodes -> 0 .. Seats]
    /\ enrolled \in 0 .. Seats
    /\ ttl \in [Nodes -> 0 .. MaxTTL]
    /\ inflight \subseteq Releases

Init ==
    /\ free = Seats
    /\ leased = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ enrolled = 0
    /\ ttl = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ inflight = {}

Lease(n, k) ==
    /\ k <= free
    /\ free' = free - k
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![n] = leased[n] + k]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![n] = MaxTTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, inflight>>

Enrol(n, k) ==
    /\ k <= leased[n]
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![n] = leased[n] - k]
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, ttl, inflight>>

SendRelease(n, k) ==
    /\ k <= leased[n]
    /\ [node |-> n, amt |-> k] \notin inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[node |-> n, amt |-> k]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, leased, enrolled, ttl>>

ApplyRelease(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ m.amt <= leased[m.node]
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![m.node] = leased[m.node] - m.amt]
    /\ free' = free + m.amt
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, ttl>>

DropRelease(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ m.amt > leased[m.node]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, leased, enrolled, ttl>>

Tick ==
    /\ \E n \in Nodes : ttl[n] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [n \in Nodes |-> IF ttl[n] > 0 THEN ttl[n] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, leased, enrolled, inflight>>

ExpireLeases ==
    /\ Lapsed # {}
    /\ free' = free + LeasedIn(Lapsed)
    /\ leased' = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n \in Lapsed THEN 0 ELSE leased[n]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, ttl, inflight>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, k \in 1 .. MaxBlock : Lease(n, k) \/ Enrol(n, k) \/ SendRelease(n, k)
    \/ \E m \in Releases : ApplyRelease(m) \/ DropRelease(m)
    \/ Tick
    \/ ExpireLeases

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EverySeatIsInExactlyOnePlace ==
    free + LeasedIn(Nodes) + enrolled = Seats
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {rn1, rn2}
    Seats = 3
    MaxBlock = 2
    MaxTTL = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT EverySeatIsInExactlyOnePlace
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A university course-registration system hands blocks of seats out to registrar nodes on leases before those seats can be turned into enrolments. Every seat in a course is always in exactly one of three states: free in the course's pool, leased to one of the registrar nodes, or enrolled to a student. Release instructions travel over a network that can reorder them freely: an instruction is put into a pool of in-flight messages and may be picked up at any later moment, in any order relative to other instructions, and possibly long after the lease it was issued under has already timed out.

The system behaves as follows. Lease moves a block of free seats into a registrar node's leased count and starts that node's lease countdown at its full value. Enrol converts some of a node's leased seats into enrolments, moving them out of the leased count and into the enrolled count. SendRelease is the node deciding to give some of its leased seats back: it puts a release instruction naming itself and a seat count into the in-flight message pool, but the seats stay leased until the instruction is actually applied. ApplyRelease picks any in-flight instruction out of the pool and applies it, moving that many seats from the named node's leased count back to the free pool; it may only fire while that node still has at least that many seats leased. DropRelease discards an in-flight instruction that the named node can no longer honour because it no longer has that many seats leased. Tick advances the clock, decrementing every lease countdown that is above zero. ExpireLeases fires when at least one node's countdown has reached zero with seats still leased, and returns all of that node's leased seats to the free pool in one step.

The reordering is what makes this delicate: an expiry can reclaim a node's seats while a release instruction for those same seats is still in flight, and applying that instruction afterwards would hand the same seats back a second time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The free seats, the seats leased to the registrar nodes, and the enrolled seats always add up to the course's fixed seat count.

---- MODULE W4Od0m3p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTerm

Vacant == "vacant"
Majority == Cardinality(Nodes) \div 2 + 1

VARIABLES term, leader, votes, ownTerm, writing

vars == <<term, leader, votes, ownTerm, writing>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {Vacant}
    /\ votes \subseteq Nodes
    /\ ownTerm \in [Nodes -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ writing \subseteq Nodes

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ ownTerm = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ writing = {}

Campaign(n) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = Vacant
    /\ votes' = {n}
    /\ ownTerm' = [ownTerm EXCEPT ![n] = term + 1]
    /\ writing' = {}

Vote(n) ==
    /\ ownTerm[n] < term
    /\ ownTerm' = [ownTerm EXCEPT ![n] = term]
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, writing>>

TakeLeadership(n) ==
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ n \in votes
    /\ ownTerm[n] = term
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Majority
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, votes, ownTerm, writing>>

StartWrite(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ ownTerm[n] = term
    /\ writing = {}
    /\ writing' = {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, votes, ownTerm>>

StopWrite(n) ==
    /\ n \in writing
    /\ writing' = writing \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, votes, ownTerm>>

StepDown(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ writing = {}
    /\ leader' = Vacant
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, votes, ownTerm, writing>>

StopWriteAny == \E n \in Nodes : StopWrite(n)

Next ==
    \E n \in Nodes :
        \/ Campaign(n) \/ Vote(n) \/ TakeLeadership(n)
        \/ StartWrite(n) \/ StopWrite(n) \/ StepDown(n)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(StopWriteAny)

OnlyTheCurrentLeaderWritesTheSchedule ==
    writing \subseteq {leader}

WritesAlwaysFinish == (writing # {}) ~> (writing = {})
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {nd1, nd2, nd3}
    MaxTerm = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheCurrentLeaderWritesTheSchedule
PROPERTY WritesAlwaysFinish
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps the day's theatre schedule in a single shared document that exactly one node may be writing at a time. Which node has that right is decided by leader election with failover: a term counter advances with each election, a node wins a term by collecting a strict majority of votes, and if the leader goes quiet another node simply starts a new term. Nodes can be slow without being failed — a node that has not heard about the latest term is still running, still able to vote, and catches up the moment it does hear.

The system behaves as follows. Campaign starts a new election: the term counter advances, the leadership of the new term begins vacant, the campaigning node adopts the new term and becomes the sole initial voter, and any write in progress is fenced off in the same step, because the whole point of starting a term is to stop the previous leader from continuing to write. Vote is a slow node catching up: a node whose own term is behind adopts the current term and joins the vote set for it. TakeLeadership makes a node in the vote set the leader of the current term, provided it is itself up to date on the term and a strict majority of the cluster has voted, and provided the term does not already have a leader. StartWrite lets the leader of the current term, which is up to date, begin writing the schedule when nobody is writing. StopWrite ends the write in progress. StepDown lets the leader give up the leadership of the current term while nobody is writing, leaving the term without a leader until someone campaigns again.

The document is corrupted the moment two hands are on it, so the schedule may only ever be written by the node that is the current term's leader, and a leader that has been displaced by a new term must stop immediately rather than finishing what it started.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of nodes writing the schedule never contains anyone other than the current term's leader.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A write in progress is always eventually finished.

---- MODULE W4Od19m6p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Titles, Branches, MaxGen

Unheld == "unheld"
NoOrder == "noorder"

VARIABLES holder, gen, order, card, network

vars == <<holder, gen, order, card, network>>

Notices == [title : Titles, by : Branches, g : 0 .. MaxGen]
Bump(k) == IF k < MaxGen THEN k + 1 ELSE k

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in [Titles -> Branches \cup {Unheld}]
    /\ gen \in [Titles -> 0 .. MaxGen]
    /\ order \in [Titles -> Branches \cup {NoOrder}]
    /\ card \in [Titles -> {"intact", "shredded"}]
    /\ network \subseteq Notices

Init ==
    /\ holder = [t \in Titles |-> Unheld]
    /\ gen = [t \in Titles |-> 0]
    /\ order = [t \in Titles |-> NoOrder]
    /\ card = [t \in Titles |-> "intact"]
    /\ network = {}

Acquire(br, t) ==
    /\ holder[t] = Unheld
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![t] = br]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, order, card, network>>

Expire(t) ==
    /\ holder[t] # Unheld
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![t] = Unheld]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![t] = Bump(gen[t])]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<order, card, network>>

IssueOrder(br, t) ==
    /\ holder[t] = br
    /\ order[t] = NoOrder
    /\ card[t] = "intact"
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![t] = br]
    /\ network' = network \cup {[title |-> t, by |-> br, g |-> gen[t]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, card>>

ReissueNotice(t) ==
    /\ order[t] # NoOrder
    /\ [title |-> t, by |-> order[t], g |-> gen[t]] \notin network
    /\ network' = network \cup {[title |-> t, by |-> order[t], g |-> gen[t]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, order, card>>

Rescind(br, t) ==
    /\ holder[t] = br
    /\ order[t] # NoOrder
    /\ card[t] = "intact"
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![t] = NoOrder]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![t] = Bump(gen[t])]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, card, network>>

DeliverNotice(m) ==
    /\ m \in network
    /\ m.g = gen[m.title]
    /\ order[m.title] = m.by
    /\ card[m.title] = "intact"
    /\ card' = [card EXCEPT ![m.title] = "shredded"]
    /\ network' = network \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, order>>

DropStaleNotice(m) ==
    /\ m \in network
    /\ m.g # gen[m.title]
    /\ network' = network \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, order, card>>

Next ==
    \/ \E br \in Branches, t \in Titles : Acquire(br, t) \/ IssueOrder(br, t) \/ Rescind(br, t)
    \/ \E t \in Titles : Expire(t) \/ ReissueNotice(t)
    \/ \E m \in Notices : DeliverNotice(m) \/ DropStaleNotice(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NothingIsShreddedWithoutAStandingOrder ==
    \A t \in Titles : (card[t] = "shredded") => (order[t] # NoOrder)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Titles = {ti1, ti2}
    Branches = {br1, br2}
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NothingIsShreddedWithoutAStandingOrder
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A library book reservation system also handles withdrawal from circulation, and shredding a title's catalogue card is irreversible — once the card is through the shredder there is no reconstructing it. A branch may only order a shredding while it holds the lease on that title's record. Leases time out on their own, and every timeout advances that title's lease generation. Shred orders travel as notices over a network that can reorder and delay them arbitrarily, so a notice issued under one lease may only surface long after that lease has gone; every notice therefore carries the lease generation it was issued under.

The system behaves as follows. Acquire gives a branch the lease on a title whose record nobody holds. Expire times a lease out: the title's record becomes unheld and its lease generation advances. IssueOrder lets the branch holding a title's lease write itself into the record as the branch that ordered the shredding, provided no order stands already, and puts a notice naming the title, itself, and the current lease generation into the network. ReissueNotice covers a notice that appears to have been lost: while an order stands, another notice for it is put into the network stamped with the title's current lease generation. Rescind lets the holding branch call the order off while the card is still intact: the recorded order is cleared and the lease generation advances, which is what makes every notice already in flight stale. DeliverNotice is the irreversible step: a notice in the network whose lease generation still matches the title's, whose named branch still matches the recorded order, and whose card is still intact, shreds the card and leaves the network. DropStaleNotice discards a notice whose lease generation no longer matches the title's.

The scenario to exclude is a notice that was issued, then overtaken by a rescission, arriving late and shredding a card that no longer has any order behind it at all.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No title's catalogue card is ever shredded unless that title's record still carries a standing shred order.

---- MODULE W4Od0m2p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Departments, MaxVersion

Versions == 0 .. MaxVersion

VARIABLES phase, acks, version, applied, network, base

vars == <<phase, acks, version, applied, network, base>>

Acks == Departments \X Versions

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "collecting", "prepared"}
    /\ acks \subseteq Departments
    /\ version \in Versions
    /\ applied \in [Versions -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ network \subseteq Acks
    /\ base \in Versions

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ acks = {}
    /\ version = 0
    /\ applied = [v \in Versions |-> FALSE]
    /\ network = {}
    /\ base = 0

BeginRound ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ phase' = "collecting"
    /\ base' = version
    /\ acks' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, applied, network>>

SendAck(d) ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ d \notin acks
    /\ <<d, base>> \notin network
    /\ network' = network \cup {<<d, base>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, acks, version, applied, base>>

ReceiveAck(m) ==
    /\ m \in network
    /\ network' = network \ {m}
    /\ acks' = IF phase = "collecting" /\ m[2] = base THEN acks \cup {m[1]} ELSE acks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, version, applied, base>>

RefuseRound ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acks, version, applied, network, base>>

Prepare ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ acks = Departments
    /\ phase' = "prepared"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acks, version, applied, network, base>>

CommitRound ==
    /\ phase = "prepared"
    /\ base = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![base] = TRUE]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acks, network, base>>

SendAny == \E d \in Departments : SendAck(d)
ReceiveAny == \E m \in Acks : ReceiveAck(m)

Next ==
    \/ BeginRound \/ RefuseRound \/ Prepare \/ CommitRound
    \/ \E d \in Departments : SendAck(d)
    \/ \E m \in Acks : ReceiveAck(m)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SendAny)
    /\ WF_vars(ReceiveAny)
    /\ WF_vars(Prepare)
    /\ WF_vars(CommitRound)

AppliedMarkersCoverExactlyTheSupersededVersions ==
    \A v \in Versions : applied[v] <=> (v < version)

OpenRoundsAlwaysClose == (phase # "idle") ~> (phase = "idle")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Departments = {dp1, dp2}
    MaxVersion = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AppliedMarkersCoverExactlyTheSupersededVersions
PROPERTY OpenRoundsAlwaysClose
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps one shared theatre record that is updated by two-phase commit across the surgical departments. Each round of the protocol is based on the record's version at the moment the round opened, and a round only commits if that base version is still current. Acknowledgements travel over a network that reorders freely, so an acknowledgement sent for one round can arrive after a later round has already opened; every acknowledgement therefore carries the base version it was sent for, and the coordinator refuses to count one whose base does not match the round now in progress. Alongside the record the scheduler keeps an applied-marker for each version, which is set when that version is superseded by a committed round.

The system behaves as follows. BeginRound opens a round while the coordinator is idle and the record still has room to advance: the round's base is set to the record's current version and the acknowledgement set starts empty. Notice that the network is not flushed, so acknowledgements left over from earlier rounds are still out there. SendAck puts one department's acknowledgement for the round in progress onto the network, provided that department has not already acknowledged this round and does not already have an acknowledgement for it in flight. ReceiveAck takes any acknowledgement off the network in any order; it counts towards the round only if the base version it carries matches the round in progress, and is otherwise simply consumed. RefuseRound is a department declining: the round in progress is abandoned and the coordinator goes idle. Prepare moves a round whose acknowledgement set covers every department into the prepared state. CommitRound applies a prepared round: the record's version advances by one and the applied-marker for the base version is set, after which the coordinator goes idle.

An update is lost if a version is superseded without being marked, or if a version at or beyond the record's current one is marked as though it had been superseded — which is what happens when a stale acknowledgement is allowed to carry a round to commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The versions carrying an applied-marker are exactly those strictly below the record's current version.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A round that has been opened is always eventually closed.

---- MODULE W4Od18m1p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RingSize, Hubs, Locks

Controllers == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Succ(i) == (i + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES token, onBus, waiting, hubOf, rekeyed

vars == <<token, onBus, waiting, hubOf, rekeyed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Controllers
    /\ onBus \subseteq Controllers
    /\ waiting \subseteq Controllers
    /\ hubOf \in [Controllers -> Hubs]
    /\ rekeyed \subseteq Locks

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ onBus = {}
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ hubOf = [c \in Controllers |-> CHOOSE h \in Hubs : TRUE]
    /\ rekeyed = {}

RequestBus(c) ==
    /\ c \notin waiting
    /\ c \notin onBus
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, onBus, hubOf, rekeyed>>

EnterBus ==
    /\ token \in waiting
    /\ onBus = {}
    /\ onBus' = {token}
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {token}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, hubOf, rekeyed>>

Rekey(lk) ==
    /\ onBus # {}
    /\ lk \notin rekeyed
    /\ rekeyed' = rekeyed \cup {lk}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, onBus, waiting, hubOf>>

LeaveBus(c) ==
    /\ c \in onBus
    /\ onBus' = onBus \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, waiting, hubOf, rekeyed>>

PassToken ==
    /\ onBus = {}
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBus, waiting, hubOf, rekeyed>>

Reassign(c, h) ==
    /\ hubOf[c] # h
    /\ hubOf' = [hubOf EXCEPT ![c] = h]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, onBus, waiting, rekeyed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : RequestBus(c) \/ LeaveBus(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, h \in Hubs : Reassign(c, h)
    \/ \E lk \in Locks : Rekey(lk)
    \/ EnterBus
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyTheTokenHolderIsOnTheBus ==
    \A c \in Controllers : (c \in onBus) => (c = token)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Hubs = {hb1, hb2}
    Locks = {lk1, lk2}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheTokenHolderIsOnTheBus
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network is managed by two independent hubs that share one pool of lock controllers; each controller answers to one hub or the other, and controllers are handed between the hubs while the house is live. All the controllers sit on a single re-keying bus, and the bus is the critical resource: no two controllers may be on it at once, because a re-key applied by two controllers at the same time leaves the locks in disagreement. Access to the bus is arbitrated by a token that circulates around the controllers in a fixed ring order.

The system behaves as follows. RequestBus lets any controller register that it wants the bus, adding itself to the set of waiting controllers. EnterBus puts the controller currently holding the token onto the bus, provided it is waiting and the bus is empty, and takes it off the waiting set. Rekey lets the controller on the bus re-key one of the shared locks, adding that lock to the set of re-keyed locks. LeaveBus takes the controller off the bus. PassToken hands the token to the next controller around the ring, and may only fire while the bus is empty, because moving the token while somebody is still on the bus would leave a controller working under an authority it no longer has. Reassign moves a controller from one hub to the other, which changes nothing about the token, the bus or the waiting set.

Note that the ring itself does not protect the bus; the token holder is merely the one allowed to step on. What keeps the bus exclusive is that the token cannot move on while the bus is occupied, so the controller on the bus is always still the token holder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any controller on the re-keying bus is the controller currently holding the ring token.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m9p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Devices, Keys, MaxEpoch, MaxAllowance

VARIABLES epoch, allowance, granted, keyEpoch, known

vars == <<epoch, allowance, granted, keyEpoch, known>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ allowance \in 0 .. MaxAllowance
    /\ granted \subseteq Keys
    /\ keyEpoch \in [Keys -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ known \in [Devices -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ allowance = MaxAllowance
    /\ granted = {}
    /\ keyEpoch = [k \in Keys |-> 0]
    /\ known = [d \in Devices |-> 0]

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ granted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allowance, keyEpoch, known>>

SyncAll ==
    /\ \E d \in Devices : known[d] < epoch
    /\ known' = [d \in Devices |-> epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, granted, keyEpoch>>

Grant(d, k) ==
    /\ known[d] = epoch
    /\ k \notin granted
    /\ Cardinality(granted) < allowance
    /\ granted' = granted \cup {k}
    /\ keyEpoch' = [keyEpoch EXCEPT ![k] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, known>>

Revoke(k) ==
    /\ k \in granted
    /\ granted' = granted \ {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, keyEpoch, known>>

SetAllowance(n) ==
    /\ n # allowance
    /\ allowance' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, granted, keyEpoch, known>>

TrimKeys ==
    /\ Cardinality(granted) > allowance
    /\ granted' = granted \ {CHOOSE k \in granted : TRUE}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allowance, keyEpoch, known>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ SyncAll
    \/ \E d \in Devices, k \in Keys : Grant(d, k)
    \/ \E k \in Keys : Revoke(k)
    \/ \E n \in 0 .. MaxAllowance : SetAllowance(n)
    \/ TrimKeys

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(TrimKeys)

OutstandingKeysBelongToTheCurrentHousehold ==
    \A k \in granted : keyEpoch[k] = epoch

AllowanceIsEventuallyHonoured ==
    (Cardinality(granted) > allowance) ~> (Cardinality(granted) <= allowance)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Devices = {dv1, dv2}
    Keys = {ky1, ky2, ky3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxAllowance = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OutstandingKeysBelongToTheCurrentHousehold
PROPERTY AllowanceIsEventuallyHonoured
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network issues digital keys to household devices. Membership of the household is managed by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: an epoch counter advances whenever the household is rebuilt, and only a device that knows the current epoch may issue a key. Every key carries the epoch it was issued under. Separately, the household's key allowance — how many keys may be outstanding at once — is changed at runtime by the account owner, and it can be set below the number of keys already outstanding.

The system behaves as follows. Reconfigure advances the epoch counter and, in the same step, revokes every outstanding key, because a key issued under the previous household is exactly what a re-keyed home must not honour. SyncAll is the household broadcast: whenever at least one device is behind, every device is brought up to the current epoch in one step. Grant issues a key: a device that knows the current epoch may hand out a key that is not already outstanding, provided the number of keys outstanding is below the current allowance, and the key is stamped with the current epoch. Revoke takes a named outstanding key back. SetAllowance changes the key allowance to any new value without touching the epoch, which is how the allowance can end up below the number of keys already outstanding. TrimKeys handles exactly that case: while the number of outstanding keys is above the allowance, one outstanding key is revoked, and it keeps happening until the household is back inside its allowance.

Two things must hold together here. No key may outlive the household it was cut for, and an allowance that has been lowered must actually come into force rather than being a number nobody honours.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every outstanding key is stamped with the current household epoch.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever more keys are outstanding than the allowance permits, the household eventually comes back within its allowance.

---- MODULE W4Od4m2p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, Slots, Bays, MaxRound

Free == "free"
NoSlot == "noslot"
Rounds == 1 .. MaxRound

VARIABLES map, mySlot, round, attempt, link, tally

vars == <<map, mySlot, round, attempt, link, tally>>

Attempts == [job : Jobs, slot : Slots, r : Rounds]
Votes == Bays \X Rounds
Live == CHOOSE a \in attempt : TRUE

TypeOK ==
    /\ map \in [Slots -> Jobs \cup {Free}]
    /\ mySlot \in [Jobs -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ round \in 0 .. MaxRound
    /\ attempt \subseteq Attempts
    /\ Cardinality(attempt) <= 1
    /\ link \subseteq Votes
    /\ tally \subseteq Bays

Init ==
    /\ map = [sl \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ mySlot = [j \in Jobs |-> NoSlot]
    /\ round = 0
    /\ attempt = {}
    /\ link = {}
    /\ tally = {}

Propose(j, sl) ==
    /\ attempt = {}
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ mySlot[j] = NoSlot
    /\ map[sl] = Free
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ attempt' = {[job |-> j, slot |-> sl, r |-> round + 1]}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<map, mySlot, link>>

CastVote(b) ==
    /\ attempt # {}
    /\ <<b, Live.r>> \notin link
    /\ b \notin tally
    /\ link' = link \cup {<<b, Live.r>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<map, mySlot, round, attempt, tally>>

CountVote(v) ==
    /\ v \in link
    /\ link' = link \ {v}
    /\ tally' = IF attempt # {} /\ v[2] = Live.r THEN tally \cup {v[1]} ELSE tally
    /\ UNCHANGED <<map, mySlot, round, attempt>>

CommitAttempt ==
    /\ attempt # {}
    /\ tally = Bays
    /\ map[Live.slot] = Free
    /\ map' = [map EXCEPT ![Live.slot] = Live.job]
    /\ mySlot' = [mySlot EXCEPT ![Live.job] = Live.slot]
    /\ attempt' = {}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, link>>

AbortAttempt ==
    /\ attempt # {}
    /\ map[Live.slot] # Free
    /\ attempt' = {}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<map, mySlot, round, link>>

FinishJob(j) ==
    /\ mySlot[j] # NoSlot
    /\ map[mySlot[j]] = j
    /\ map' = [map EXCEPT ![mySlot[j]] = Free]
    /\ mySlot' = [mySlot EXCEPT ![j] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, attempt, link, tally>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, sl \in Slots : Propose(j, sl)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : CastVote(b)
    \/ \E v \in Votes : CountVote(v)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : FinishJob(j)
    \/ CommitAttempt
    \/ AbortAttempt

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

JobSlotRecordsAgreeWithTheConveyorMap ==
    \A j \in Jobs : (mySlot[j] # NoSlot) => (map[mySlot[j]] = j)
====
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line allocates numbered conveyor slots to wash jobs, and a slot is only bound to a job after a two-phase commit across the bay controllers. The coordinator runs one attempt at a time, and every attempt carries a round number taken from a counter that advances with each new attempt. Votes come back over a link that reorders freely, so a vote cast for an earlier attempt can turn up during a later one; each vote therefore carries the round number it was cast for, and a vote whose round does not match the attempt in progress is thrown away rather than counted. Both the conveyor's own slot map and each job's record of the slot it holds are kept, and they must agree.

The system behaves as follows. Propose opens an attempt when none is in progress: the round counter advances, and the attempt records a job that currently holds no slot together with a slot the conveyor map shows as free. CastVote puts one bay controller's vote for the attempt in progress onto the link, stamped with that attempt's round number, provided a vote from that controller for that round is not already in flight. CountVote takes any vote off the link in any order; it joins the tally only if its round number matches the attempt in progress, and is otherwise discarded. CommitAttempt binds the slot when every bay controller's vote has been counted and the conveyor map still shows the slot as free: the map records the job and the job's record gains the slot, and the attempt closes with an empty tally. AbortAttempt closes the attempt without binding anything when the conveyor map no longer shows the slot as free, which is how a race for the same slot is resolved. FinishJob releases a job's slot, clearing it from the job's record and from the conveyor map together.

Two jobs on one slot is the collision the whole protocol exists to prevent, and it shows up the instant a job's record of the slot it holds disagrees with the conveyor's slot map.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot a job records as its own is recorded by the conveyor map as belonging to that same job.

CONSTANTS Banks

Ungranted == "ungranted"

VARIABLES grant, writing, round, tally, lagging

vars == <<grant, writing, round, tally, lagging>>

Candidate == CHOOSE b \in round : TRUE

TypeOK ==
    /\ grant \in Banks \cup {Ungranted}
    /\ writing \subseteq Banks
    /\ round \subseteq Banks
    /\ Cardinality(round) <= 1
    /\ tally \subseteq Banks
    /\ lagging \subseteq Banks

Init ==
    /\ grant = Ungranted
    /\ writing = {}
    /\ round = {}
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ lagging = {}

OpenRound(b) ==
    /\ round = {}
    /\ grant = Ungranted
    /\ round' = {b}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, writing, lagging>>

CastVote(b) ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ b \notin lagging
    /\ b \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, writing, round, lagging>>

ToggleSlow(b) ==
    /\ lagging' = IF b \in lagging THEN lagging \ {b} ELSE lagging \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, writing, round, tally>>

CommitGrant ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ tally = Banks
    /\ grant' = Candidate
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<writing, lagging>>

AbortRound ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ tally # Banks
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, writing, lagging>>

    /\ writing = {}
    /\ writing' = {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, round, tally, lagging>>

LeaveLedger(b) ==

    /\ writing' = writing \ {b}
    /\ grant' = Ungranted

        \/ CommitGrant \/ AbortRound

    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(LeaveAny)

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bk1, bk2, bk3}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheGrantHolderWritesTheLedger
PROPERTY LedgerWritersAlwaysLeave
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch writes into a single settlement ledger, and the ledger is a critical resource: exactly one member bank may be writing to it at a time. The right to write is not taken, it is granted, and it is granted only by a two-phase commit round in which every member bank votes. Member banks can be slow without being failed: a bank may drop into a lagging state where it is still up and still part of the membership but is not answering votes for the moment, and it comes back on its own.

The system behaves as follows. OpenRound starts a commit round when no round is in flight and the write right is not currently granted, naming the bank that wants it and starting with an empty tally. CastVote records the vote of a member bank that is not lagging and has not yet voted in this round. ToggleSlow flips a bank between the responsive state and the lagging state, which is what makes a round stall without anybody having failed. CommitGrant closes a round in which every member bank has voted, handing the write right to the bank the round named. AbortRound abandons a round that has not yet collected every vote, clearing the tally and leaving the write right ungranted, which is how the batch escapes a round stalled behind a lagging bank. EnterLedger puts the bank holding the write right into the ledger, provided nobody is in there. LeaveLedger takes the bank out of the ledger and gives the write right back up in the same step, so a bank cannot step out and step back in without winning another round.

Because the write right is surrendered together with leaving the ledger, and a new round cannot even open while the right is granted, the only bank that can ever be inside the ledger is the one the last successful round named.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bank writing to the settlement ledger is the bank currently holding the write right.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A bank writing to the settlement ledger always eventually leaves it.

CONSTANTS Operators, Feeders, MaxOverrides

VARIABLES certified, voters, ballot, shed, overrides

vars == <<certified, voters, ballot, shed, overrides>>

UnderBallot == CHOOSE f \in ballot : TRUE

TypeOK ==
    /\ certified \subseteq Operators
    /\ voters \subseteq Operators
    /\ ballot \subseteq Feeders
    /\ Cardinality(ballot) <= 1
    /\ shed \subseteq Feeders
    /\ overrides \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ certified = Operators
    /\ voters = {}
    /\ ballot = {}
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ overrides = MaxOverrides

Certify(o) ==
    /\ o \notin certified
    /\ certified' = certified \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voters, ballot, shed, overrides>>

Decertify(o) ==
    /\ o \in certified
    /\ certified' = certified \ {o}
    /\ voters' = voters \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, shed, overrides>>

OpenBallot(f) ==
    /\ ballot = {}
    /\ f \notin shed
    /\ ballot' = {f}
    /\ voters' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<certified, shed, overrides>>

Vote(o) ==
    /\ ballot # {}
    /\ o \in certified
    /\ o \notin voters
    /\ voters' = voters \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<certified, ballot, shed, overrides>>

ShedByQuorum ==
    /\ ballot # {}
    /\ Cardinality(voters) * 2 > Cardinality(certified)
    /\ voters # {}
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {UnderBallot}
    /\ ballot' = {}
    /\ voters' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<certified, overrides>>

AdminShed(f) ==
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ f \notin shed
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {f}
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<certified, voters, ballot>>

Restore(f) ==
    /\ f \in shed
    /\ shed' = shed \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<certified, voters, ballot, overrides>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Operators : Certify(o) \/ Decertify(o) \/ Vote(o)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : OpenBallot(f) \/ AdminShed(f) \/ Restore(f)
    \/ ShedByQuorum

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StandingVotesComeFromCertifiedOperators == voters \subseteq certified
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Operators = {op1, op2, op3}
    Feeders = {fd1, fd2}
    MaxOverrides = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StandingVotesComeFromCertifiedOperators
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A power-grid load shedder decides which feeders to drop during an emergency by quorum voting among the control-room operators. Only operators who hold a current certification may vote, and certification is granted and withdrawn while the grid is running. A privileged system-operator override also exists, which can drop a feeder without any ballot at all, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. Certify adds an operator to the set of currently certified operators. Decertify withdraws an operator's certification and, in the same step, strikes that operator's vote from any ballot in progress, because a vote cast by someone who is no longer certified must not be allowed to stand and be counted. OpenBallot starts a ballot on a feeder that is not already shed, when no ballot is in progress, with an empty set of voters. Vote records a currently certified operator's vote on the ballot in progress; no operator votes twice in the same ballot. ShedByQuorum drops the feeder under ballot once a strict majority of the currently certified operators have voted, clearing the ballot and the voters. AdminShed is the privileged path: the system operator drops any feeder outright, spending one unit of override budget and touching no ballot. Restore brings a shed feeder back into service.

The point of striking votes on decertification is that the quorum is measured against the operators certified right now; if a stale vote could linger on a ballot, a feeder could be dropped on the authority of somebody the control room has already stood down.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every vote standing on the ballot in progress belongs to an operator who is currently certified.

Unclaimed == "unclaimed"
Task == "task"
Queues == UNION { [1 .. n -> {Task}] : n \in 0 .. Capacity }

VARIABLES queue, backlog, assigned, onDock, claim

vars == <<queue, backlog, assigned, onDock, claim>>

    /\ queue \in Queues
    /\ backlog \in 0 .. MaxBacklog
    /\ assigned \in 0 .. MaxAssigned
    /\ onDock \subseteq Services
    /\ claim \in Services \cup {Unclaimed}

    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ backlog = MaxBacklog
    /\ assigned = 0
    /\ onDock = {}
    /\ claim = Unclaimed

Submit ==
    /\ backlog > 0
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, Task)
    /\ backlog' = backlog - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, onDock, claim>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, onDock, claim>>

ClaimDock(s) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, backlog, assigned, onDock>>

    /\ onDock = {}
    /\ onDock' = {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, backlog, assigned, claim>>

CONSTANTS
    Services = {sv1, sv2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxBacklog = 2
    MaxAssigned = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheClaimHolderStandsOnTheDock
PROPERTY TheQueueAlwaysDrains
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked by two independent restocking services that draw work from one shared pool of machines. Restock tasks are queued in a bounded work queue with backpressure: once the queue is at capacity nothing further is queued until the dispatcher drains one. The depot's loading dock is a critical resource — only one service may be on the dock at a time — and a service gets on the dock by first claiming it and then stepping onto it.

The system behaves as follows. Submit takes one machine off the backlog of machines needing attention and appends a restock task to the tail of the queue, and requires the queue to be below capacity. TakeHead is the dispatcher: it removes the task at the head of the queue and adds it to the count of tasks assigned but not yet carried out, a count that saturates at its maximum rather than growing without bound. ClaimDock lets a service claim the loading dock while it is unclaimed. EnterDock puts the service holding the claim physically onto the dock, provided the dock is clear. Restock is the work itself: the service standing on the dock carries out one assigned task, decreasing the assigned count. LeaveDock takes the service off the dock and releases its claim in the same step, so a service cannot step off and step back on while still holding the claim.

Note that the dispatcher does not need the dock: draining the queue and working the dock are separate concerns, which is what lets the queue keep moving even while the two services are contending for the dock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any service standing on the loading dock is the service that currently holds the dock claim.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The restock queue is always eventually empty.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Services, NumClaims, MaxVersion, Float

Idle == 0
Claims == 1 .. NumClaims

VARIABLES version, refunded, drawer, workingOn, readVersion

vars == <<version, refunded, drawer, workingOn, readVersion>>

RECURSIVE Value(_)
Value(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN x + Value(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in [Claims -> 0 .. MaxVersion]
    /\ refunded \subseteq Claims
    /\ drawer \in 0 .. Float
    /\ workingOn \in [Services -> Claims \cup {Idle}]
    /\ readVersion \in [Services -> 0 .. MaxVersion]

Init ==
    /\ version = [c \in Claims |-> 0]
    /\ refunded = {}
    /\ drawer = Float
    /\ workingOn = [s \in Services |-> Idle]
    /\ readVersion = [s \in Services |-> 0]

Read(s, c) ==
    /\ workingOn[s] = Idle
    /\ c \notin refunded
    /\ workingOn' = [workingOn EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![s] = version[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, refunded, drawer>>

CommitRefund(s) ==
    /\ workingOn[s] # Idle
    /\ readVersion[s] = version[workingOn[s]]
    /\ version[workingOn[s]] < MaxVersion
    /\ drawer >= workingOn[s]
    /\ refunded' = refunded \cup {workingOn[s]}
    /\ drawer' = drawer - workingOn[s]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![workingOn[s]] = version[workingOn[s]] + 1]
    /\ workingOn' = [workingOn EXCEPT ![s] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED readVersion

Conflict(s) ==
    /\ workingOn[s] # Idle
    /\ readVersion[s] # version[workingOn[s]]
    /\ workingOn' = [workingOn EXCEPT ![s] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, refunded, drawer, readVersion>>

ReviseClaim(c) ==
    /\ version[c] < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![c] = version[c] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<refunded, drawer, workingOn, readVersion>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Services, c \in Claims : Read(s, c)
    \/ \E s \in Services : CommitRefund(s) \/ Conflict(s)
    \/ \E c \in Claims : ReviseClaim(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TheDrawerBalancesAgainstTheRefunds ==
    drawer + Value(refunded) = Float
====

CONSTANTS
    Services = {sv1, sv2}
    NumClaims = 2
    MaxVersion = 2
    Float = 4
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TheDrawerBalancesAgainstTheRefunds
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network settles customer refund claims out of a single cash drawer, and two independent settlement services work the same pool of claims. Paying a refund is irreversible: the cash is gone. Neither service locks anything; they use optimistic locking with retry against a per-claim version number. A service reads a claim and the version it is at, and only pays out if that version is still what it read. Every payout advances the claim's version, and a claim's record can also be revised independently, which advances the version too. Claims are numbered, and a claim's number is also the amount of cash it pays out.

The system behaves as follows. Read has an idle service pick up a claim that has not yet been refunded, recording both the claim and the version number it saw. CommitRefund is the irreversible payout: the service pays out when the version it recorded still matches the claim's current version and the drawer holds at least that much cash; the claim joins the set of refunded claims, the cash leaves the drawer, the claim's version advances, and the service goes idle. Conflict is the losing side of a race: a service whose recorded version no longer matches the claim's current version drops the claim and goes idle without paying anything. ReviseClaim is the independent edit path: a claim's record is amended, which advances its version and thereby invalidates any read a service is holding on it.

The books are the check on all of this. The drawer started with a known float, and every cash movement out of it corresponds to exactly one claim joining the refunded set. If both services managed to pay the same claim, the drawer would be short by that claim's amount while the refunded set stayed exactly the same size.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The cash left in the drawer plus the total amount of the refunded claims always equals the drawer's opening float.

Job == "job"

Grants == Collectors \X (1 .. MaxGen)

VARIABLES queue, holder, inSafe, genNo, link

    /\ holder \in Collectors \cup {Unheld}
    /\ inSafe \subseteq Collectors
    /\ genNo \in 0 .. MaxGen
    /\ link \subseteq Grants

    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ holder = Unheld
    /\ inSafe = {}
    /\ genNo = 0
    /\ link = {}

QueueJob ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, Job)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inSafe, genNo, link>>

TakeJob ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inSafe, genNo, link>>

IssueGrant(c) ==
    /\ holder = Unheld
    /\ genNo < MaxGen
    /\ genNo' = genNo + 1
    /\ link' = link \cup {<<c, genNo + 1>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, holder, inSafe>>

DeliverGrant(g) ==
    /\ g \in link
    /\ g[2] = genNo
    /\ holder = Unheld
    /\ holder' = g[1]
    /\ link' = link \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inSafe, genNo>>

    /\ \/ g[2] # genNo
       \/ holder # Unheld
    /\ link' = link \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, holder, inSafe, genNo>>

    /\ holder = c
    /\ inSafe = {}
    /\ inSafe' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, holder, genNo, link>>

    /\ c \in inSafe
    /\ inSafe' = inSafe \ {c}
    /\ holder' = Unheld
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, genNo, link>>

DropAny == \E g \in Grants : DropStaleGrant(g)

Next ==
    \/ QueueJob
    \/ TakeJob
    \/ \E c \in Collectors : IssueGrant(c) \/ OpenSafe(c) \/ CloseSafe(c)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : DeliverGrant(g) \/ DropStaleGrant(g)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(DeliverAny \/ DropAny)

OnlyTheSafeHolderIsInside ==
    \A c \in inSafe : holder = c

TheRadioLinkAlwaysClears == (link # {}) ~> (link = {})
====

CONSTANTS
    Collectors = {cl1, cl2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheSafeHolderIsInside
PROPERTY TheRadioLinkAlwaysClears
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending machine network sends collectors out to empty coin boxes. Collection jobs sit in a bounded work queue with backpressure — nothing is queued once the queue is at capacity — and the depot safe, where the coin bags are counted in, is a critical resource that only one collector may be inside at a time. The right to open the safe is granted by dispatch as a message, and dispatch messages travel over a radio link that reorders and delays them freely. Each grant therefore carries a generation number, dispatch advances the generation with every grant it issues, and only a grant carrying the generation currently in force is honoured.

The system behaves as follows. QueueJob appends a collection job to the tail of the work queue and requires the queue to be below capacity. TakeJob removes the job at the head of the queue and hands it to the collectors. IssueGrant has dispatch advance the grant generation and put a grant addressed to a chosen collector, stamped with the new generation, onto the radio link; dispatch will only do this while nobody holds the safe. DeliverGrant honours a grant that is still current and finds the safe unheld: the addressed collector becomes the holder and the grant leaves the link. DropStaleGrant discards a grant from the link whose generation is no longer the one in force, or that arrives when the safe is already held. OpenSafe puts the current holder inside the safe when the safe is empty. CloseSafe takes the collector out of the safe and gives up the holding in the same step, so the collector needs a fresh grant to go back in.

The reordering is the hazard: an old grant addressed to a different collector can surface at any time, and honouring it would put a second collector inside the safe alongside the first.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any collector inside the depot safe is the collector who currently holds the safe.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every dispatch grant left on the radio link is eventually taken off it.

CONSTANTS RingSize, Packs, MaxOverrides

Suites == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Succ(i) == (i + 1) % RingSize

    /\ mode \in [Suites -> {"idle", "queued", "using"}]

    /\ sterile = {}

    /\ mode[s] = "idle"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![s] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sterile, overrides>>

GrabHoist(s) ==
    /\ mode[s] = "queued"
    /\ s = token
    /\ ~InUse
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![s] = "using"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sterile, overrides>>

FinishHoist(s) ==
    /\ mode[s] = "using"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sterile, overrides>>

SterilisePack(pk) ==
    /\ InUse
    /\ pk \notin sterile
    /\ sterile' = sterile \cup {pk}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, mode, overrides>>

PassToken ==
    /\ ~InUse
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, sterile, overrides>>

ChargeNurseOverride(s) ==
    /\ ~InUse
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ s # token
    /\ token' = s
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, sterile>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Suites : RequestHoist(s) \/ GrabHoist(s) \/ FinishHoist(s) \/ ChargeNurseOverride(s)
    \/ \E pk \in Packs : SterilisePack(pk)
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Packs = {pk1, pk2}
    MaxOverrides = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TheSuiteOnTheHoistHoldsTheToken
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler arbitrates the sterile-supply hoist between the theatre suites. The hoist is a critical resource: at most one suite may be on it, because two suites drawing from it at once mixes their instrument trays. Arbitration is by a token that circulates around the suites in a fixed ring order. A privileged charge-nurse override exists that can hand the token directly to a named suite out of ring order, for emergencies, and its budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. RequestHoist moves an idle suite into the queued state, meaning it wants the hoist. GrabHoist moves the suite holding the token from queued into the using state, which is the state of actually being on the hoist. FinishHoist moves a suite from using back to idle. SterilisePack lets the suite currently using the hoist put one instrument pack through the steriliser, adding it to the set of sterile packs. PassToken advances the token to the next suite around the ring, and may only fire while no suite is in the using state, because the whole protection rests on the token not moving out from under a suite that is on the hoist. ChargeNurseOverride hands the token straight to a named suite, spending one unit of override budget, and it too may only fire while no suite is using the hoist.

Both ways of moving the token are blocked while a suite is on the hoist, so a suite in the using state is always still the token holder; if either of them could fire mid-use, the next holder could climb onto the hoist alongside the current one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any theatre suite in the using state is the suite currently holding the ring token.

Sessions == [inst : Instances, by : Operators, base : 0 .. MaxVersion]
Open == CHOOSE e \in session : TRUE

    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
    /\ session \subseteq Sessions
    /\ Cardinality(session) <= 1
    /\ valid \subseteq Operators
    /\ applied \in 0 .. MaxApplied
    /\ retries \in 0 .. MaxRetries

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ session = {}
    /\ valid = Operators
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ retries = 0

OpenEdit(i, o) ==
    /\ session = {}
    /\ o \in valid
    /\ session' = {[inst |-> i, by |-> o, base |-> version]}
    /\ retries' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, valid, applied>>

RevokeBadge(o) ==
    /\ o \in valid
    /\ valid' = valid \ {o}
    /\ session' = {e \in session : e.by # o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, applied, retries>>

ReinstateBadge(o) ==
    /\ o \notin valid
    /\ valid' = valid \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, session, applied, retries>>

ExternalBump ==
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, valid, applied, retries>>

Retry ==
    /\ session # {}
    /\ Open.base # version
    /\ retries < MaxRetries
    /\ session' = {[inst |-> Open.inst, by |-> Open.by, base |-> version]}
    /\ retries' = retries + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, valid, applied>>

CommitEdit ==
    /\ session # {}
    /\ Open.base = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ applied' = IF applied < MaxApplied THEN applied + 1 ELSE applied
    /\ session' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<valid, retries>>

AbortEdit ==
    /\ session # {}
    /\ \/ Open.base # version
       \/ version = MaxVersion
    /\ session' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, valid, applied, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, o \in Operators : OpenEdit(i, o)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : RevokeBadge(o) \/ ReinstateBadge(o)
    \/ ExternalBump \/ Retry \/ CommitEdit \/ AbortEdit

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(CommitEdit \/ AbortEdit)

OpenSessionsRestOnValidBadges ==

OpenSessionsAlwaysEnd == (session # {}) ~> (session = {})

CONSTANTS
    Instances = {in1, in2}
    Operators = {op1, op2}
    MaxVersion = 2
    MaxApplied = 2
    MaxRetries = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OpenSessionsRestOnValidBadges
PROPERTY OpenSessionsAlwaysEnd
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line keeps its wash programs in one shared configuration pool, and two independent scheduling instances edit that pool. There is no lock: edits use optimistic locking with retry against the pool's version number, and the pool admits one edit session at a time. An edit may only be opened by an operator whose badge is currently valid, and badges are revoked and reinstated while the line is running, which is how an operator becomes stale mid-edit.

The system behaves as follows. OpenEdit starts a session when the pool has no session open, recording the instance running it, the operator who authorised it, and the pool version that operator read; the operator's badge must be valid at that moment. RevokeBadge withdraws an operator's badge and, in the same step, tears down any edit session that operator authorised, because a session carrying a withdrawn badge must not be allowed to sit there and later commit. ReinstateBadge gives a badge back. ExternalBump models the other instance landing a change into the shared pool: the pool version advances, which silently invalidates the version any open session read. Retry re-bases an open session whose recorded version has fallen behind, taking the current version and spending one unit of the session's retry allowance. CommitEdit applies a session whose recorded version still matches the pool's and where the pool can still advance: the version advances and the applied-edit tally goes up, saturating at its maximum. AbortEdit tears a session down when its recorded version no longer matches, or when the pool version can no longer advance.

Between commit and abort, one of the two always applies to an open session, so no session can sit open forever; and because revocation tears sessions down on the spot, no session ever rests on a badge that has been withdrawn.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every open edit session was authorised by an operator whose badge is still valid.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An open edit session is always eventually torn down.

EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Surgeons, Slots, Capacity, MaxDropped

Free == "free"

VARIABLES queue, board, fabric, held, dropped

vars == <<queue, board, fabric, held, dropped>>

Requests == [sur : Surgeons, slot : Slots]
Queues == UNION { [1 .. n -> Requests] : n \in 0 .. Capacity }
Cur == queue[1]

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Queues
    /\ board \in [Slots -> Surgeons \cup {Free}]
    /\ fabric \subseteq Requests
    /\ held \in [Surgeons -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ dropped \in 0 .. MaxDropped

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ board = [sl \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ fabric = {}
    /\ held = [su \in Surgeons |-> {}]
    /\ dropped = 0

Enqueue(su, sl) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [sur |-> su, slot |-> sl])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, fabric, held, dropped>>

ServeHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ board[Cur.slot] = Free
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![Cur.slot] = Cur.sur]
    /\ fabric' = fabric \cup {Cur}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, dropped>>

RejectHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ board[Cur.slot] # Free
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ dropped' = IF dropped < MaxDropped THEN dropped + 1 ELSE dropped
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, fabric, held>>

DeliverConfirmation(m) ==
    /\ m \in fabric
    /\ board[m.slot] = m.sur
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m.sur] = held[m.sur] \cup {m.slot}]
    /\ fabric' = fabric \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, board, dropped>>

Release(su, sl) ==
    /\ board[sl] = su
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![sl] = Free]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![su] = held[su] \ {sl}]
    /\ fabric' = fabric \ {[sur |-> su, slot |-> sl]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, dropped>>

Next ==
    \/ \E su \in Surgeons, sl \in Slots : Enqueue(su, sl) \/ Release(su, sl)
    \/ \E m \in Requests : DeliverConfirmation(m)
    \/ ServeHead
    \/ RejectHead

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ConfirmationsInFlightAgreeWithTheBoard ==
    \A m \in fabric : board[m.slot] = m.sur
====

CONSTANTS
    Surgeons = {su1, su2}
    Slots = {sl1, sl2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxDropped = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ConfirmationsInFlightAgreeWithTheBoard
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler takes booking requests into a bounded work queue with backpressure — nothing is accepted once the queue is at capacity — and serves them strictly in arrival order against the theatre board. When a booking is served, a confirmation is put out to the requesting surgeon over a messaging fabric that reorders and delays freely, so a confirmation can be sitting in the fabric long after the board has moved on. Each surgeon also keeps a personal list of the slots they have been confirmed for.

The system behaves as follows. Enqueue appends a booking request naming a surgeon and a theatre slot to the tail of the queue, and requires the queue to be below capacity. ServeHead handles the request at the head of the queue when the board shows its slot free: the board records the surgeon, a confirmation naming that surgeon and slot goes out onto the fabric, and the request leaves the queue. RejectHead handles the request at the head when the board shows its slot already taken: the request is simply dropped from the queue and the dropped-request tally advances, saturating at its maximum. DeliverConfirmation takes a confirmation off the fabric in any order and, provided the board still shows that slot as belonging to that surgeon, adds the slot to the surgeon's personal list. Release gives up a slot: the board is cleared, the slot leaves the holding surgeon's personal list, and any confirmation for that surgeon and slot still sitting in the fabric is withdrawn in the same step.

That last withdrawal is the crux. A confirmation left in the fabric after its slot has been released would, on delivery, put the slot into a surgeon's list while the board could already have given it to someone else — the same slot allocated twice.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every confirmation still in the messaging fabric names a surgeon that the theatre board currently shows as holding that confirmation's slot.

vars == <<term, instTerm, round, votes, filled>>

Live == CHOOSE r \in round : TRUE

    /\ instTerm \in [Instances -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ round \subseteq Rounds
    /\ Cardinality(round) <= 1
    /\ votes \subseteq Approvers
    /\ filled \subseteq Seats

    /\ instTerm = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ round = {}
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ filled = {}

RotateTerm ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}

SyncBoth ==

    /\ instTerm' = [i \in Instances |-> term]

OpenRound(i, se) ==

    /\ instTerm[i] = term
    /\ se \notin filled
    /\ round' = {[by |-> i, seat |-> se, t |-> term]}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, instTerm, filled>>

CastVote(a) ==

    /\ a \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, instTerm, round, filled>>

CommitRound ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ votes = Approvers
    /\ filled' = filled \cup {Live.seat}
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, instTerm>>

    /\ round # {}
    /\ votes # Approvers
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, instTerm, filled>>

    \/ RotateTerm \/ SyncBoth \/ CommitRound \/ AbandonRound
    \/ \E i \in Instances, se \in Seats : OpenRound(i, se)
    \/ \E a \in Approvers : CastVote(a)

    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SyncBoth)

    \A r \in round : r.t = term

    (\E i \in Instances : instTerm[i] < term) ~> (\A i \in Instances : instTerm[i] = term)

nl:
A university course-registration system is fronted by two independent registration instances that share one pool of course seats. Seats are only filled by a two-phase commit across the departmental approvers, and the pool admits one commit round at a time. The registry rotates a term number whenever the catalogue is republished, and a round is bound to the term it was opened in; an instance may only open a round while it knows the current term.

The system behaves as follows. RotateTerm advances the registry's term number and, in the same step, tears down any round in flight, because a round opened against the previous catalogue must not be allowed to complete against the new one. SyncBoth is the registry broadcast: whenever at least one instance is behind, both instances are brought up to the current term in a single step. OpenRound starts a round when the pool has none in flight: the instance opening it must know the current term, the seat it names must not already be filled, and the round records the instance, the seat and the current term. CastVote records the vote of a departmental approver who has not yet voted in the round in flight. CommitRound fills the seat once every approver has voted, closing the round and clearing the votes. AbandonRound closes a round that has not collected every vote yet, clearing the votes and leaving the seat unfilled.

Because the term rotation tears rounds down rather than letting them ride, and because opening a round requires knowing the current term, no round in flight is ever bound to a superseded catalogue — which is exactly what it would mean for a stale front-end to be acting on the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any round in flight is bound to the registry's current term.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever either registration instance is behind on the term, both instances eventually know the current term.

---- MODULE W4Od7m6p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Containers, Cranes, Instances, MaxTTL

VARIABLES stack, hold, ship, ttl, managedBy

vars == <<stack, hold, ship, ttl, managedBy>>

Lapsed == {cr \in Cranes : ttl[cr] = 0 /\ hold[cr] # {}}

RECURSIVE HeldCount(_)
HeldCount(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN Cardinality(hold[x]) + HeldCount(S \ {x})

RECURSIVE HeldBy(_)
HeldBy(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN {}
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN hold[x] \cup HeldBy(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ stack \subseteq Containers
    /\ hold \in [Cranes -> SUBSET Containers]
    /\ ship \subseteq Containers
    /\ ttl \in [Cranes -> 0 .. MaxTTL]
    /\ managedBy \in [Cranes -> Instances]

Init ==
    /\ stack = Containers
    /\ hold = [cr \in Cranes |-> {}]
    /\ ship = {}
    /\ ttl = [cr \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ managedBy = [cr \in Cranes |-> CHOOSE i \in Instances : TRUE]

LiftFromStack(cr, k) ==
    /\ k \in stack
    /\ stack' = stack \ {k}
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![cr] = hold[cr] \cup {k}]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![cr] = MaxTTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, managedBy>>

LoadToShip(cr, k) ==
    /\ k \in hold[cr]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![cr] = hold[cr] \ {k}]
    /\ ship' = ship \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, ttl, managedBy>>

ReturnToStack(cr, k) ==
    /\ k \in hold[cr]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![cr] = hold[cr] \ {k}]
    /\ stack' = stack \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, ttl, managedBy>>

Tick ==
    /\ \E cr \in Cranes : ttl[cr] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [cr \in Cranes |-> IF ttl[cr] > 0 THEN ttl[cr] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, hold, ship, managedBy>>

ExpireLeases ==
    /\ Lapsed # {}
    /\ stack' = stack \cup HeldBy(Lapsed)
    /\ hold' = [cr \in Cranes |-> IF cr \in Lapsed THEN {} ELSE hold[cr]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, ttl, managedBy>>

Reassign(cr, i) ==
    /\ managedBy[cr] # i
    /\ managedBy' = [managedBy EXCEPT ![cr] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, hold, ship, ttl>>

Next ==
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, k \in Containers : LiftFromStack(cr, k) \/ LoadToShip(cr, k) \/ ReturnToStack(cr, k)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, i \in Instances : Reassign(cr, i)
    \/ Tick
    \/ ExpireLeases

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TheYardCensusAlwaysAddsUp ==
    Cardinality(stack) + HeldCount(Cranes) + Cardinality(ship) = Cardinality(Containers)
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is run by two independent yard-management instances that share one pool of containers. A container is always in exactly one of three places: sitting in the stack, held by a crane, or loaded onto the ship. A crane does not own containers outright; it holds them under a lease with a countdown, and when the countdown runs out everything that crane is holding goes straight back to the stack, because a crane that has gone quiet must not be allowed to sit on yard inventory indefinitely. Each crane is managed by one of the two instances, and cranes are handed between the instances while the yard is working.

The system behaves as follows. LiftFromStack takes one container out of the stack into a crane's hold and restarts that crane's lease countdown at its full value. LoadToShip moves one container from a crane's hold onto the ship. ReturnToStack puts one container from a crane's hold back into the stack. Tick advances the yard clock, decrementing every crane's countdown that is still above zero. ExpireLeases fires whenever at least one crane has run its countdown to zero while still holding containers, and in one step returns everything held by every such crane to the stack. Reassign hands a crane from one management instance to the other, which moves no containers at all.

The yard's census is the check. Every step here moves a container between exactly two of the three places and never creates or destroys one, so the containers in the stack, the containers in the cranes' holds, and the containers on the ship must always come to the yard's full complement — an expiry that emptied a crane's hold without putting the containers back in the stack would lose inventory outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The containers in the stack, the containers held by the cranes, and the containers loaded on the ship always come to the yard's full complement.

    /\ carLock \in [Cars -> Technicians \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ used \subseteq Cars
    /\ inRoom \subseteq Technicians
    /\ roomDone \in BOOLEAN
    /\ crashed \subseteq Technicians

    /\ bankLock = Nobody
    /\ carLock = FreeCars
    /\ used = {}
    /\ inRoom = {}
    /\ roomDone = FALSE
    /\ crashed = {}

AcquireBank(t) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ bankLock = Nobody
    /\ bankLock' = t
    /\ used' = {}
    /\ roomDone' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carLock, inRoom, crashed>>

AcquireCar(t, c) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ bankLock = t
    /\ carLock[c] = Nobody
    /\ c \notin used
    /\ carLock' = [carLock EXCEPT ![c] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, used, inRoom, roomDone, crashed>>

ReleaseCar(t, c) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ carLock[c] = t
    /\ carLock' = [carLock EXCEPT ![c] = Nobody]
    /\ used' = used \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, inRoom, roomDone, crashed>>

EnterRoom(t) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ bankLock = t
    /\ inRoom = {}
    /\ ~roomDone
    /\ inRoom' = {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, carLock, used, roomDone, crashed>>

LeaveRoom(t) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ t \in inRoom
    /\ inRoom' = inRoom \ {t}
    /\ roomDone' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, carLock, used, crashed>>

    /\ inRoom = {}
    /\ \A c \in Cars : carLock[c] # t

    /\ UNCHANGED <<carLock, used, inRoom, roomDone, crashed>>

    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, carLock, used, inRoom, roomDone>>

    /\ bankLock' = Nobody
    /\ carLock' = FreeCars
    /\ inRoom' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, roomDone, crashed>>

    \/ \E t \in Technicians, c \in Cars : ReleaseCar(t, c)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians : ReleaseBank(t) \/ LeaveRoom(t)
    \/ ForceRelease

    \/ \E t \in Technicians : AcquireBank(t) \/ EnterRoom(t) \/ LeaveRoom(t) \/ ReleaseBank(t) \/ Crash(t)

    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    Technicians = {tc1, tc2}
    Cars = {ca1, ca2}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheBankLockHolderIsInTheMachineRoom
PROPERTY TheBankLockIsAlwaysGivenBack
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper lets technicians into the machine room, which is a critical resource: only one technician may be in there, because the brake test they run there acts on the whole bank. Entry is protected by a two-level lock hierarchy — a technician must first hold the single bank lock, and only then may it take the lock on an individual car. A technician can crash silently, stopping work with no notice while still holding everything it has taken, so the building system carries a watchdog that can force the whole hierarchy open.

The system behaves as follows. AcquireBank gives an uncrashed technician the bank lock when it is free, starting a fresh session in which no car has yet been used and the machine room has not yet been visited. AcquireCar gives the technician holding the bank lock the lock on a free car, provided that car has not already been used and given back during this session. ReleaseCar gives back a car lock the technician holds and records that car as used for the rest of the session. EnterRoom puts the technician holding the bank lock into the machine room, provided the room is empty and the room has not already been visited during this session. LeaveRoom takes the technician out of the machine room and marks the room as visited for the rest of the session. ReleaseBank gives back the bank lock, and requires that the technician holds no car locks and that the machine room is empty. Crash silently disables a technician, after which it can acquire, release, enter and leave nothing. ForceRelease is the watchdog: when the bank lock is held by a technician that has crashed, it tears the whole hierarchy down at once — the bank lock and every car lock are released and the machine room is cleared.

Because the room can only be entered by the bank-lock holder and the bank lock cannot be handed on while the room is occupied, at most one technician is ever in the machine room; the watchdog is what stops a crashed holder from making that "at most one" mean "exactly one, forever".

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any technician in the machine room is the technician currently holding the bank lock.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The bank lock, once taken, is always eventually free again.

    /\ aisleLock = r
    /\ boxLock[b] = Nobody
    /\ boxLock' = [boxLock EXCEPT ![b] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleLock, contents, manifest, sealed, overrides>>

LoadPallet(r, b, p) ==
    /\ boxLock[b] = r
    /\ b \notin sealed
    /\ ~Placed(p)
    /\ contents' = [contents EXCEPT ![b] = contents[b] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleLock, boxLock, manifest, sealed, overrides>>

Seal(r, b) ==
    /\ boxLock[b] = r
    /\ b \notin sealed
    /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {b}
    /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![b] = contents[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleLock, boxLock, contents, overrides>>

DispatcherSeal(b) ==
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ b \notin sealed
    /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {b}
    /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![b] = contents[b]]
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleLock, boxLock, contents>>

ReleaseContainer(r, b) ==
    /\ boxLock[b] = r
    /\ boxLock' = [boxLock EXCEPT ![b] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleLock, contents, manifest, sealed, overrides>>

ReleaseAisle(r) ==
    /\ aisleLock = r
    /\ \A b \in Containers : boxLock[b] # r
    /\ aisleLock' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boxLock, contents, manifest, sealed, overrides>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : AcquireAisle(r) \/ ReleaseAisle(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Containers : AcquireContainer(r, b) \/ Seal(r, b) \/ ReleaseContainer(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Containers, p \in Pallets : LoadPallet(r, b, p)
    \/ \E b \in Containers : DispatcherSeal(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SealedManifestsMatchTheirContents ==
    \A b \in sealed : manifest[b] = contents[b]
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet loads outbound containers under a two-level lock hierarchy: a robot must hold the aisle lock before it may take the lock on any container in that aisle. Sealing a container is irreversible — once the seal is on, the container goes on the truck and nothing more can be put in it — and sealing freezes the container's manifest, which is the shipping document stating what is inside. A privileged dispatcher override can seal a container without any lock being held at all, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. AcquireAisle gives a robot the aisle lock when it is free. AcquireContainer gives the robot holding the aisle lock the lock on a container nobody holds. LoadPallet lets the robot holding a container's lock put a pallet into that container, provided the container is not already sealed and the pallet is not already sitting in some container. Seal is the irreversible act: the robot holding a container's lock seals it, and the manifest is written to be exactly the contents at that instant. DispatcherSeal is the privileged path: an unsealed container is sealed outright with its manifest written from its contents, spending one unit of override budget and holding no lock. ReleaseContainer gives back a container lock the robot holds. ReleaseAisle gives back the aisle lock, and requires the robot to be holding no container lock.

The manifest is the whole point of sealing being once-only. If a container could be loaded again after sealing, or sealed a second time over different contents, the document on the outside of the box would stop describing what is inside it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every sealed container's manifest lists exactly the pallets that container actually holds.

CONSTANTS Drones, Extensions, MaxVersion, MaxPerimeter

NoRead == -1

VARIABLES version, perimeter, revisions, held, slow

vars == <<version, perimeter, revisions, held, slow>>

Entries == (0 .. MaxVersion) \X Extensions
Stale == {d \in Drones : held[d] # NoRead /\ held[d] # version}

RECURSIVE Total(_)
Total(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET e == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN e[2] + Total(S \ {e})

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
    /\ perimeter \in 0 .. MaxPerimeter
    /\ revisions \subseteq Entries
    /\ held \in [Drones -> (0 .. MaxVersion) \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ slow \subseteq Drones

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ perimeter = 0
    /\ revisions = {}
    /\ held = [d \in Drones |-> NoRead]
    /\ slow = {}

TakeReading(d) ==
    /\ d \notin slow
    /\ held[d] = NoRead
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![d] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, perimeter, revisions, slow>>

LandUpdate(d, e) ==
    /\ held[d] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ perimeter + e <= MaxPerimeter
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ perimeter' = perimeter + e
    /\ revisions' = revisions \cup {<<version, e>>}
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![d] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED slow

SweepStaleReads ==
    /\ Stale # {}
    /\ held' = [d \in Drones |-> IF d \in Stale THEN NoRead ELSE held[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, perimeter, revisions, slow>>

ToggleSlow(d) ==
    /\ slow' = IF d \in slow THEN slow \ {d} ELSE slow \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, perimeter, revisions, held>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : TakeReading(d) \/ ToggleSlow(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, e \in Extensions : LandUpdate(d, e)
    \/ SweepStaleReads

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SweepStaleReads)

    perimeter = Total(revisions)

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {dr1, dr2}
    Extensions = {1, 2}
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxPerimeter = 5
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ThePerimeterMatchesTheRevisionLog
PROPERTY StaleReadsAreAlwaysSweptAway
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm maintains one shared fire-perimeter record. The record carries a length and a version number, and drones update it with a compare-and-swap: a drone reads the version, works out how much to extend the perimeter, and its update only lands if the version it read is still the version on the record. Every landed update advances the version by one and is written into an append-only revision log as the version it superseded together with the extension it applied. Drones can be slow without being failed — a slow drone is still flying and still reporting, it simply is not reading the record for the moment — and the swarm runs a periodic sweep that discards every read that has gone out of date.

The system behaves as follows. TakeReading has a drone that is not currently slow and is not already holding a read record the record's current version. LandUpdate is the compare-and-swap: a drone whose held read still matches the record's version extends the perimeter by its amount, the version advances, a revision-log entry pairing the superseded version with the extension is written, and the drone's read is cleared. SweepStaleReads is the periodic sweep: whenever at least one drone is holding a read that no longer matches the record's version, every such out-of-date read is cleared in a single step, leaving up-to-date reads alone. ToggleSlow flips a drone between reporting and slow, which is what stops it taking readings for a while without it having failed.

An update is lost if the perimeter moves without the revision log recording the move, or if the log records a move the perimeter never took. Because the compare-and-swap serialises the landings, the log and the perimeter are two accounts of the same sequence of extensions and must always agree.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The recorded perimeter length always equals the total of all the extensions written in the revision log.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever any drone is holding an out-of-date read, the swarm eventually holds no out-of-date reads at all.

vars == <<batchLock, acctLock, authorised, posted, overrides>>
