    /\ acctLock \in [Accounts -> Clerks \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ authorised \subseteq Clerks
    /\ posted \subseteq Accounts
    /\ overrides \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ batchLock = Nobody
    /\ acctLock = [a \in Accounts |-> Nobody]
    /\ authorised = Clerks
    /\ posted = {}
    /\ overrides = MaxOverrides

AcquireBatch(k) ==
    /\ k \in authorised
    /\ batchLock = Nobody
    /\ batchLock' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acctLock, authorised, posted, overrides>>

AcquireAccount(k, a) ==
    /\ batchLock = k
    /\ acctLock[a] = Nobody
    /\ acctLock' = [acctLock EXCEPT ![a] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, authorised, posted, overrides>>

PostEntry(k, a) ==
    /\ acctLock[a] = k
    /\ a \notin posted
    /\ posted' = posted \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, acctLock, authorised, overrides>>

ReleaseAccount(k, a) ==
    /\ acctLock[a] = k
    /\ acctLock' = [acctLock EXCEPT ![a] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, authorised, posted, overrides>>

ReleaseBatch(k) ==
    /\ batchLock = k
    /\ \A a \in Accounts : acctLock[a] # k
    /\ batchLock' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acctLock, authorised, posted, overrides>>

Withdraw(k) ==
    /\ k \in authorised
    /\ authorised' = authorised \ {k}
    /\ batchLock' = IF batchLock = k THEN Nobody ELSE batchLock
    /\ acctLock' = [a \in Accounts |-> IF acctLock[a] = k THEN Nobody ELSE acctLock[a]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, overrides>>

SupervisorPost(a) ==
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ a \notin posted
    /\ posted' = posted \cup {a}
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, acctLock, authorised>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Clerks : AcquireBatch(k) \/ ReleaseBatch(k) \/ Withdraw(k)
    \/ \E k \in Clerks, a \in Accounts : AcquireAccount(k, a) \/ PostEntry(k, a) \/ ReleaseAccount(k, a)
    \/ \E a \in Accounts : SupervisorPost(a)

    \A a \in Accounts : (acctLock[a] # Nobody) => (acctLock[a] \in authorised)

CONSTANTS
    Clerks = {ck1, ck2}
    Accounts = {ac1, ac2}
    MaxOverrides = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AccountLocksAreHeldByAuthorisedClerks
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is posted by clerks working under a two-level lock hierarchy: a clerk must hold the single batch lock before it may take the lock on an individual account. Authorisation to post is granted and withdrawn while the batch is running, and withdrawing a clerk's authorisation is a hard stop — it strips that clerk of every lock it is holding, the batch lock included, in the same step. A privileged supervisor override can post to an account without holding any lock at all, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. AcquireBatch gives an authorised clerk the batch lock when it is free. AcquireAccount gives the clerk holding the batch lock the lock on an account nobody holds. PostEntry lets the clerk holding an account's lock post that account into the batch. ReleaseAccount gives back an account lock the clerk holds. ReleaseBatch gives back the batch lock, and requires the clerk to be holding no account locks. Withdraw removes a clerk's authorisation and simultaneously releases the batch lock if that clerk holds it and every account lock that clerk holds, so nothing is left standing in the name of a clerk who has been stood down. SupervisorPost is the privileged path: an account is posted into the batch outright with no lock held, spending one unit of override budget.

The hierarchy on its own does not stop a withdrawn clerk from carrying on; what does is that withdrawal takes the locks away at the same instant. If a stripped clerk could keep an account lock, it would keep the right to post to that account long after the bank had revoked its authority.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every account lock that is held is held by a clerk who is still authorised.

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxVersion, MaxTTL

Nobody == "nobody"
NoBase == -1
Versions == 0 .. MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, author, holder, base, ttl

vars == <<version, author, holder, base, ttl>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in Versions
    /\ author \in [Versions -> Nodes \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ holder \in Nodes \cup {Nobody}
    /\ base \in Versions \cup {NoBase}
    /\ ttl \in 0 .. MaxTTL

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ author = [v \in Versions |-> Nobody]
    /\ holder = Nobody
    /\ base = NoBase
    /\ ttl = 0

TakeLease(n) ==
    /\ holder = Nobody
    /\ holder' = n
    /\ base' = version
    /\ ttl' = MaxTTL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, author>>

Commit ==
    /\ holder # Nobody
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ base = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ author' = [author EXCEPT ![version] = holder]
    /\ holder' = Nobody
    /\ base' = NoBase
    /\ UNCHANGED ttl

Rebase ==
    /\ holder # Nobody
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ base # version
    /\ base' = version
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, author, holder, ttl>>

Tick ==
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ ttl' = ttl - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, author, holder, base>>

ExpireLease ==
    /\ holder # Nobody
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ holder' = Nobody
    /\ base' = NoBase
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, author, ttl>>

SeizeLease ==
    /\ holder # Nobody
    /\ holder' = Nobody
    /\ base' = NoBase
    /\ ttl' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, author>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : TakeLease(n)
    \/ Commit \/ Rebase \/ Tick \/ ExpireLease \/ SeizeLease

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Tick)
    /\ WF_vars(ExpireLease)

AuthorshipCoversExactlyTheSupersededVersions ==
    \A v \in Versions : (author[v] # Nobody) <=> (v < version)

TheLeaseIsAlwaysGivenBack == (holder # Nobody) ~> (holder = Nobody)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {nd1, nd2}
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxTTL = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AuthorshipCoversExactlyTheSupersededVersions
PROPERTY TheLeaseIsAlwaysGivenBack
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps a master theatre schedule that is edited under a lease. A node takes the lease, makes its change against the version it read, and commits; the lease carries a countdown, and when the countdown runs out the lease is taken back whether or not the holder ever committed. Every committed change advances the schedule's version by one and writes the committing node into the authorship record for the version it superseded. A privileged duty-manager override can seize the lease from whoever holds it.

The system behaves as follows. TakeLease gives a node the lease when it is free, starting the countdown at its full value and recording the version the node read as its base. Commit applies a change: the node holding the lease, whose recorded base still matches the schedule's version and whose countdown has not run out, advances the version by one and writes itself into the authorship record for the version it just superseded; the lease is given up in the same step. Rebase lets the holder whose base has fallen behind pick up the current version and try again without giving up the lease. Tick advances the clock, decrementing the countdown while it is above zero. ExpireLease takes the lease back once the countdown has reached zero, discarding whatever the holder was working on. SeizeLease is the privileged path: the duty manager takes the lease away from its current holder outright, leaving it free.

An update is lost when a version is superseded without anybody being recorded as its author, or when the authorship record claims a version that the schedule has not actually passed. Because commit does both things in one step and no other step touches either, the authorship record and the version counter are two views of the same history.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The versions with a recorded author are exactly those the schedule has already advanced past.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A held lease on the master schedule is always eventually free again.

---- MODULE W4Od9m6p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, Rated, Headroom, MaxBlock, MaxTTL, MaxOverrides

VARIABLES load, alloc, ttl, overrides

vars == <<load, alloc, ttl, overrides>>

Lapsed == {f \in Feeders : ttl[f] = 0 /\ alloc[f] > 0}

RECURSIVE Sum(_)
Sum(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN alloc[x] + Sum(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in 0 .. Rated + Headroom
    /\ alloc \in [Feeders -> 0 .. Rated + Headroom]
    /\ ttl \in [Feeders -> 0 .. MaxTTL]
    /\ overrides \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ load = 0
    /\ alloc = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ ttl = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ overrides = MaxOverrides

Allocate(f, n) ==
    /\ load + n <= Rated
    /\ load' = load + n
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![f] = alloc[f] + n]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![f] = MaxTTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED overrides

ShedBlock(f, n) ==
    /\ n <= alloc[f]
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![f] = alloc[f] - n]
    /\ load' = load - n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, overrides>>

Tick ==
    /\ \E f \in Feeders : ttl[f] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [f \in Feeders |-> IF ttl[f] > 0 THEN ttl[f] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, alloc, overrides>>

ExpireLeases ==
    /\ Lapsed # {}
    /\ load' = load - Sum(Lapsed)
    /\ alloc' = [f \in Feeders |-> IF f \in Lapsed THEN 0 ELSE alloc[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, overrides>>

EmergencyRedispatch(f, n) ==
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ n <= Rated
    /\ load' = n
    /\ alloc' = [g \in Feeders |-> IF g = f THEN n ELSE 0]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![f] = MaxTTL]
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, n \in 1 .. MaxBlock : Allocate(f, n) \/ ShedBlock(f, n) \/ EmergencyRedispatch(f, n)
    \/ Tick
    \/ ExpireLeases

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TotalLoadStaysWithinTheRatedImport == load <= Rated
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {fd1, fd2}
    Rated = 3
    Headroom = 2
    MaxBlock = 2
    MaxTTL = 1
    MaxOverrides = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TotalLoadStaysWithinTheRatedImport
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A power-grid load shedder allocates import capacity to feeders. The interconnector has a hard rated import, and the total load carried across all feeders must never exceed it. Capacity is not owned by a feeder permanently: it is allocated under a lease with a countdown, and when a feeder's countdown runs out its whole allocation is handed back to the pool, because a feeder whose controller has gone quiet must not be allowed to hold import capacity forever. A privileged control-room override exists for emergency re-dispatch, and its budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. Allocate gives a feeder an additional block of import capacity, and requires the total load afterwards to stay within the rated import; the feeder's countdown is restarted at its full value. ShedBlock takes a block of capacity back off a feeder that holds at least that much, lowering the total load. Tick advances the clock, decrementing every feeder's countdown that is still above zero. ExpireLeases fires whenever at least one feeder has run its countdown to zero while still holding capacity, and returns everything held by every such feeder in one step, lowering the total load accordingly. EmergencyRedispatch is the privileged path: the control room drops every feeder's allocation to nothing and gives one named feeder a block within the rated import, spending one unit of override budget; because it clears the board first, the emergency block is always inside the rating.

The rated import is the thing that must hold through all of it — through partial sheds, through several leases expiring together, and through an emergency re-dispatch that rewrites the whole allocation in a single step.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total load allocated across all feeders never exceeds the interconnector's rated import.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, MaxTerm, MaxEntries

Vacant == "vacant"
Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm
Ballots == Servers \X Terms
Majority == Cardinality(Servers) \div 2 + 1

VARIABLES term, leader, tally, voteTerm, link, entries

vars == <<term, leader, tally, voteTerm, link, entries>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in Terms
    /\ leader \in Servers \cup {Vacant}
    /\ tally \subseteq Servers
    /\ voteTerm \in [Servers -> Terms]
    /\ link \subseteq Ballots
    /\ entries \in 0 .. MaxEntries

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ voteTerm = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ link = {}
    /\ entries = 0

Campaign(s) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = Vacant
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ voteTerm' = [voteTerm EXCEPT ![s] = term + 1]
    /\ link' = link \cup {<<s, term + 1>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED entries

SendVote(s) ==
    /\ s \notin tally
    /\ <<s, term>> \notin link
    /\ voteTerm' = [voteTerm EXCEPT ![s] = term]
    /\ link' = link \cup {<<s, term>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, tally, entries>>

CountVote(v) ==
    /\ v \in link
    /\ link' = link \ {v}
    /\ tally' = IF v[2] = term THEN tally \cup {v[1]} ELSE tally
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, voteTerm, entries>>

TakeLeadership(s) ==
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ s \in tally
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Majority
    /\ leader' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, tally, voteTerm, link, entries>>

PostBatch ==
    /\ leader # Vacant
    /\ entries < MaxEntries
    /\ entries' = entries + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, tally, voteTerm, link>>

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # Vacant
    /\ leader' = Vacant
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, tally, voteTerm, link, entries>>

CountAny == \E v \in Ballots : CountVote(v)

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Campaign(s) \/ SendVote(s) \/ TakeLeadership(s)
    \/ \E v \in Ballots : CountVote(v)
    \/ PostBatch \/ StepDown

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(CountAny)

TheTallyHoldsOnlyCurrentTermVotes ==
    \A s \in tally : voteTerm[s] = term

TheLinkAlwaysDrains == (link # {}) ~> (link = {})
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Servers = {sv1, sv2, sv3}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxEntries = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TheTallyHoldsOnlyCurrentTermVotes
PROPERTY TheLinkAlwaysDrains
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch runs on a cluster of settlement servers with leader election and failover. Only the leader of the current term may post to the batch. Election messages travel over a link that reorders and delays freely, so a vote cast in an earlier term can arrive in the middle of a later one; every vote message therefore carries the term it was cast for, and a vote whose term does not match the term now running is thrown away rather than counted.

The system behaves as follows. Campaign starts a new term: the term counter advances, the leadership of the new term begins vacant, the tally is emptied, and the campaigning server puts its own vote for the new term onto the link. SendVote puts one server's vote for the current term onto the link, provided that server does not already have a vote for that term in flight and has not already been counted. CountVote takes any vote message off the link, in any order: it joins the tally only if the term it carries is the term now running, and is otherwise consumed and discarded. TakeLeadership makes a server that has been counted the leader of the current term, provided a strict majority has been counted and the term has no leader yet. PostBatch lets the leader of the current term post an entry into the settlement batch. StepDown vacates the leadership of the current term.

The tally is what authorises a leader, so the tally must never contain anything but votes cast for the term actually running; a vote that drifted in from an earlier term would let a server claim a majority it never had, and post to the batch on stale authority.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every vote standing in the tally was cast for the term currently running.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every vote message left on the link is eventually taken off it.

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line finishes cars with a hot-wax coat drawn from a single drum. Applying the wax is irreversible — the coat is on, it cannot be taken off, and a second coat would draw a second measure out of the drum. Several finishing bays work the line at once and none of them locks anything: they use optimistic locking with retry against each car's record version. A bay reads a car and the version it is at, and its application only goes ahead if that version is still current; every application advances the car's version, as does an independent revision of the car's record. A privileged shift-manager override can wax a car outright without reading anything, and its budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. ReadCar has an idle bay pick up a car that has not been waxed, recording the car and the version it saw. ApplyWax is the irreversible act: the bay applies the coat when the version it recorded still matches the car's current version, the drum has at least one measure left, and the car's version can still advance; the car joins the waxed set, one measure leaves the drum, the car's version advances and the bay goes idle. Conflict is the losing side of a race: a bay whose recorded version no longer matches drops the car and goes idle without applying anything. ReviseCar amends a car's record independently, advancing its version and thereby invalidating any read a bay is holding on it. ManagerWax is the privileged path: an unwaxed car whose version can still advance is waxed outright, one measure leaves the drum, the car's version advances and one unit of override budget is spent.

The drum is the audit trail. It started full, and exactly one measure leaves it for each car that joins the waxed set. Two bays both waxing the same car would take two measures out for one car, and the drum would come up short against the waxed set — which is precisely the double coat the version check exists to prevent.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The measures left in the wax drum plus the number of cars that have been waxed always equal the drum's starting measures.
